previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes, morbid obesity, atrial fibrillation, and prior right hallux amputation for gas gangrene was admitted due to new erythema and yellow drainage around his surgical wound. He was evaluated for possible recurrent infection but found to have no fever, leukocytosis, or radiographic signs of osteomyelitis or soft tissue gas. The changes were attributed to benign healing changes and increased granulation tissue. Podiatry performed a bedside debridement and determined no acute surgical or infectious intervention was needed. The patient remained stable, continued on oral augmentin, and was discharged home the following day with instructions to follow up for wound grafting and monitor for signs of infection.

He reports a weight gain of 10 lbs in the last few weeks;

home. He does not reliably report PND or orthopnea. He reported 
some jaw discomfort since yesterday which is resolving.

negative ~7L during this admission. He is breathing on room air.

that he has had stable lower extremity edema and occasional

in the setting of holding torsemide for two days, but have 
otherwise been stable during this admission. He is requesting a 
lasix gtt as soon as possible, reporting that he had 70 lbs of

around 315 lbs, but he does not weigh himself at home. He denies 
salty food intake and reports medication adherence.

He also complains of crusting along the eyelid margins and 
bilateral ocular irritation, reporting a prior diagnosis of

Brief Hospital Course:
Podiatry Service Discharge summary:
The patient was admitted to the hospital preoperatively for a 
split thickness skin graft procedure from his right thigh to 
foot on ___.  Preoperative workup was completed and pt was 
kept NPO at ___ for the operation the next day. Pt was started on 
all his home medications except coumadin which was held until 
after the procedure.  Pt was kept on lovenox as eventual 
bridging therapy when he restarted his coumadin POD2.  The 
patient was also restarted on his lasix as he incorrectly 
stopped taking it three days prior to admission. On ___, 
HD2, pt was evaluated by anesthesia and taken to the operating 
room.  Please, see the operative note for details.  During the 
operation, pt had oxygen saturations down to the high ___.  
Afterwards, pt was taken to the PACU in stable condition, then 
transferred to the ward for observation. 

After surgery, patient had several brief episodes of shortness 
of breathe when lying down likely secondary to being fluid 
overloaded.  His oxygen saturation decreased to the low ___ and 
respiratory rate up to the low ___. Therefore, his lasix dose 
was increased to 60mg instead of a range between 40-60mg.  Pt 
also had a cough and therefore a chest xray was performed on HD2 
which had concern for PNA.  
The medicine team was consulted for management. They agreed with 
60mg of lasix but did not agree the pt had PNA.  Therefore, 
antibiotics were not started.

Pain was well controlled with oral pain medication on a PRN 
basis.  Early and frequent ambulation were encouraged while 
remaining nonweightbearing to his right leg.  A bi-valve cast 
was made for the patient to further protect and offload his 
right foot graft site.

Eventually, the heart failure team transferred him to their 
service for management.  Below is their discharge summary:

Active issues:

# Acute on chronic HFrEF: Given that he does not weigh himself

___ edema and orthopnea, which were likely exacerbated in the

___ per day. Home medications of ACE-i, spironolactone, and a 
beta-blocker were continued. He was monitored on telemetry 
(notable for frequent PVCs and NSVT), and his electrolytes were 
repleted as needed. He was counseled on a low sodium diet. His 
ECHO showed LVEF 35%, and it was noted that he may benefit from 
ICD in the future. Additionally, he may benefit from cardiac MRI 
to further assess his diagnosis of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy 
once he is euvolemic and can lay flat. 

# Atrial fibrillation: Given his history of stroke and CHADS2 
score of 5 suggesting high risk of future stroke, he was bridged 
till therapeutic with INR in ___ range. His home dose of 
warfarin is 5mg daily, and was prescribed 4 mg at the time of 
discharge.

# R hallux ulcer s/p amputation, debridement, and closure with 
skin graft: Stable per podiatry with no further surgical 
interventions needed per their assessment at the time of 
transfer. During his time on the heart failure service, he was 
reassessed by the podiatry team with no further recommendations. 
Patient was afebrile without evidence of systemic infection. He 
was encouraged to adhere to the instruction to be 
nonweightbearing on the RLE and to follow up with podiatry as 
scheduled.
 
# Blepharitis: A chronic problem ___ meibomian gland dysfunction 
(clogged oil glands in lid margins) and likely poor hygeine in 
context of hospitalization. Patient has struggled with ocular 
irritation for over ___ years. He continued to complain of eye 
irritation daily, and was evaluated by ophthalmology, who 
recommended artificial tears, cyclosporine eye drops, and 
artificial tear ointment. He was instructed about the importance 
of gentle facial cleansing with baby shampoo and application of 
warm compresses. His home medication of fish oil 3000 BID was 
continued, as the patient reports that this helps. He was also 
treated with a dose of ivermectin for possible demodex 
folliculorum. Ophthalmology recommended restasis and artificial 
tears (ointment and drops)which the patient had variable 
adherence to. He was also found to be wiping his eyes with 
betadyne wipes intended for foot dressing changes. 

Chronic issues:
# Type 2 Diabetes: Stable. Hemoglobin a1c in ___ was 8.6. He 
was treated with ISS, Glargine, and a diabetic diet while 
inpatient. On discharge, he was restarted on his home Novolin 30

Activity Status: Ambulatory - Independent.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital to have a skin graft and 
closure of your foot and were found to have a lot of edema. You 
were transferred to the cardiology service to receive diuretics. 
You lost a significant amount of weight and your swelling 
improved. 

You are now ready to be discharged. Please follow up with the 
providers listed below and adhere to the post-surgery 
instructions below from the podiatry service.

These are the discharge instructions for post-operative 
discharge instructions. 

Discharge Instructions: Please call your surgeon or return to 
the emergency department if you develop a fever greater than 
101.5, severe increase in pain to operative site or pain 
unrelieved by your pain medication, nausea, vomiting, chills, 
foul smelling or colorful drainage from your incisions/wounds, 
redness or swelling around your incisions, or any other symptoms 
which are concerning to you.

Activity:
Please, remain nonweightbearing to your right forefoot. This is 
crucial to increase healing potential.

Wound Care:
You may shower but please keep dressings clean, dry, and intact. 
 Do not submerge your foot/leg in water. 
Please call the doctor or page the ___ pager, if you have 
increased pain, swelling, redness, or drainage to the operative 
sites.

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.

We wish you the best, 
Your ___ Care Team
